main_body: two-story Japanese machiya building with tiled roof and lattice ground floor
top_band: slate-blue tiled roof ridge and slope, rows 0-30 (plus secondary awning roof at rows 41-46)
evidence: Rows 0-30 show the foreshortened top slope and ridge of the kawara tile roof with a distinct highlight along the front eave edge (rows 29-30) and dark eave shadow beneath (rows 31-32). Below are the plaster upper wall with inset mushiko-mado windows (rows 33-40), a lower tiled awning (rows 41-46) with its own eave shadow (row 47), and the ground-floor wooden lattice facade and recessed doorway with noren curtains (rows 48-78).

style.evidence: The roof tiles have 5-6 slate-blue value steps with individual tile scallops and highlights. The upper plaster wall has subtle speckle texture and recessed window frames. The lower wooden lattice, noren curtains, and bamboo inuyarai guards are richly detailed with multi-step shading and dark material-toned outlines matching the Beodeul reference standard.
